## Utility usefulness and creative application

Apply this standard before offering a new Utility from any source, including class kits, Signatures and Talents, and when the player requests a Utility revision. Every required Utility slot needs reliable value in ordinary noncombat play. Preserve its source, honestly fixed rarity, acquisition rules and the existing number of powers.

### Define a capability the player can use

Start with what the character can do and the recurring decisions it supports, then give that operation a class-specific method, appearance and limits. Manipulating materials, interpreting traces, finding routes or influencing communication are possible directions, not a required menu or a list of finished powers. Keep the class identity and originality gates. Adding more prerequisites does not establish originality, and a large maximum effect does not compensate for a capability that almost never applies.

An Active Utility should normally let the player initiate a useful action with resources they can reasonably obtain, carry or encounter in the established setting. A Passive should provide a persistent capability or operate during common activities such as examining, travelling, negotiating or handling objects. A material requirement may express the class when that material is ordinarily available. Do not make baseline usefulness depend on a named location, rare species, unusual disaster, exact sequence of events or encounter invented to support the power. Do not assume routine equipment damage, missing evidence or other unrecorded problems just to create a use.

When an unusual circumstance gives the power its exceptional benefit, preserve a meaningful ordinary application of the same underlying capability. A restoration power might perform a larger or more lasting task under special conditions while retaining a useful everyday scope. This does not require every Utility to have both Active and Passive modes, or permit an unrelated extra activation. An explicitly requested narrow specialization remains possible after its limited ordinary use is clear to the player.

### Give improvisation clear boundaries

State what the capability affects, its permitted operation, scale, reach, time, cost and relevant constraints. Examples explain applications within those rules; they are not an exhaustive permission list. Judge a new application by the same operation and limits. A plausible application still follows the normal checks, risks, resistance and consequences; it does not grant automatic success, free resources, hidden knowledge or an unlisted power. Rarity may increase practical breadth, reliability or scale under its existing power contract. Keep all existing Active/Passive distinctions and out-of-combat restrictions.

### Check usefulness before publishing

Before releasing a Utility, establish THREE concrete, plausible uses across at least TWO different kinds of noncombat problem. Travel or access, investigation, communication, and practical work or logistics are examples of problem types, not compulsory categories for every class. Each use must change a meaningful choice or outcome through the actual written mechanics. Repairing a gate, an arch and a statue counts as one repair function; changing the object name alone does not establish different uses. Test ordinary situations supported by public world facts and at least one plausible use beyond the immediate starting set piece. Do not invent a future encounter, new faction, missing fragments or convenient failure to make the test pass, and do not reveal undiscovered information to justify the power.

Compare the proposed Utility with the character's other class powers and owned capabilities. Multiple Utilities must cover different recurring needs; a larger repair limit or longer duration alone does not create a second practical function. Check the whole kit for overlap before broadening a narrow power, so a revision does not duplicate an existing construction, investigation or travel ability. The GM performs this check before publication without burdening the player with internal validation labels or a long design report.

If the power fails, redesign its underlying capability at the SAME fixed rarity and within the same source and slot before offering it. Preserve published offers and saved powers until the player authorizes a mechanical revision. A revision keeps the recorded identity, source and rarity, states the changed mechanics, and follows the campaign's normal save and approval rules. Loading this amendment alone does not replace an owned ability, reroll an offer or advance the campaign.
